The Wempe Einheits-Chronometer model · verification · 29 October 2026 · the Hamilton's: would a chronometer made to it run?, the model against real Model 21s

The Wempe Einheits-Chronometer: does the model hold to its drawings, and would it keep time?

The model of the German standard marine chronometer of the 1940s is built from Wempe's works drawings, each sheet as last revised. Two questions follow from that. Does the model hold to its drawings: is every part a closed solid where its sheets put it, clear of its neighbours, counted against the drawing list, every figure read and every guess said to be one? And would a chronometer made to those drawings keep time: does the escapement run, does the fusee even the spring, does the energy budget close, do the teeth and springs hold, does it stay in rate from cold to hot and at sea, and does it pass the trial its Soviet copy, the 6MX, was made to pass? Every figure below comes from a script in the repository, run on the model's own numbers, and is shown as the script prints it: ok a check that holds, ~~ one the script reports but doesn't fail on (an open question, or the strong end of a range only), !! a failure.

Approach

The Wempe's checks are the Hamilton's, pointed at the second model (--model wempe), with tools of their own where the two chronometers differ: the Wempe's detent carries a gold passing spring on its own horn, its fusee's force was measured by its makers on the drawing itself, its balance is a cut bimetallic one with movable masses, and its hairspring is a helix with drawn terminal curves. The tools run on the same files the page draws from (js/escapement.js, js/escphys.js, the shared makeEsc), so what they check is what the page shows.

#QuestionMethodScript
1Is every part a sound solid, clear of its neighbours, and on the drawing list?Closed-mesh tests, a 0.05 mm voxel interference check through the escapement's phases and the wind, a screw and loose-end audit, the Spread view's clearance, every part against bom.jsonsolids.py, fine.py, audit.py, exploded.py, bom.py
2What do the drawings say, and what had to be guessed?The sheets transcribed figure by figure with how sure each reading is; the readings corrected on the sheets; the estimates listedReferences/wempe/, the model's README
3Does the escapement run, and does it run in time as the averaged model says?makeEsc solved from the layout drawing; the escapement integrated beat by beat; the detent as a frame of beam elementswempe_escapement.js, dynamics.js, tripping.js
4Does the drawn fusee even the mainspring as its makers measured?The spring solved for its shape at every quarter turn, fitted in length and set to 05 06_20's forcewempe_mainspring.py
5Is there energy enough, from spring to balance?Every loss from the parts, the balance's damping from its parts; the swing the drive can holdwempe_physics.js
6Do the gears mesh, and how exactly must the holes be placed?Tooth-by-tooth contact on the page's own outlines; the train in time; each mesh's depthing windowgearing.js
7Will the loaded parts hold, fully wound?Each part's stress against its material's published rangewempe_strength.js
8Does the drawn hairspring keep the balance free of side forces, and isochronous?Phillips' conditions on 05 03_7's curve; the spring at large swings as an elastica and as beam elementswempe_hairspring.js
9Does the bimetallic balance compensate, and where must the masses sit?The rim's quarters as bimetal cantilevers, every part weighed; the secondary errorwempe_thermal.js, wempe_thermal_frame.js
10Does the case hang level and stay so at sea?The case and ring weighed on the model, levelled as 05 01 says, run in a seawaymassprops.py, gimbals.js
11Would it pass the 6MX's trial, and what would a navigator carry?The TU's 35-day trial and a 60-day voyage, Monte Carlo over the rate's partswempe_errorbudget.js
12Would a Wempe made to its drawings work, and how is it tested?The unsized parts' tolerances from the escapement's swing over the wind; the bench's tests with their pass figures; 2,000 movements made to tolerances, as made and after the benchwempe_tolerances.js, wempe_bench.js, wempe_montecarlo.js
13How does the escapement compare with a period text's rules?Each proportion against Watch and Clock Escapements (1904), Ch. III; reported, never judgedkeystone.js
14Is the balance's damping right?A running 6MX's swing read frame by frame off a video, fitted with the Wempe's balance equationwempe_swing.py, wempe_startup.js

Units: millimetres and micrometres (µm), newtons, seconds a day (s/d, + gaining). The swing is the balance's amplitude, each way. The model runs its balance at the train's half second; the drawn hairspring with the weighed balance gives a little less (section 8), which a maker times out. A rate of 4 s of time is a mile of longitude at the equator. Each tool's whole output is under its checks ("its whole output"), as it printed it when this page was built.

1. Geometry: does the model hold to its drawings?

The model is a set of closed solids, as a CAD model is, so it can be checked as one. Five browser checks open the Wempe's page itself and measure the parts as built. Solids: every mesh closed (no open edge), consistently wound and with a positive volume, as loaded and in a section with Moving parts only. Fine interference: every part voxelized at 0.05 mm in states (the escapement through its unlocking, impulse and return; the train at many phases; the fusee from full wind through winding to run down), every pair of parts that overlaps reported; only the contacts listed below, each with its reason and a size it may not exceed, may overlap. The screw audit: screws overlapping, screws with nothing under their heads, arbor and pin ends sitting in nothing, faces lying on each other, parts touching nothing, in the movement and in the case and box, against the leftovers expected. Exploded: the Spread view lifts each part on its own path; no two may pass through each other. The parts list: every line of bom.json, transcribed from the drawing list, counted on the model's pieces, and its relations measured on the built meshes.

The contacts that are meant

Every overlap fine.py finds is one of these, each a joint the drawings make that a turned or extruded solid can't show cut: a screw in a thread not cut across a turned body, a pressed fit drawn at its fit's middle, the chain in its groove. The measured column is the largest overlap over all the states, against the size it may reach.

The audit's expected leftovers

The parts list

2. The sources: what the drawings say, and what was guessed

The model's evidence is, in order: the works drawings (sheets of Wempe's, as published by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Chronometrie, each read as last revised); the coloured section of the whole movement; photographs of real German movements (Wempe 3955 above all); and, for what only the Soviet copy shows, the 6MX's own documents. None of them is reproduced here: they are other people's work, cited and linked from the model's page. The model's README says for every figure which sheet it is from and how sure the reading is; below is that record in numbers.

The sheets

The transcription

Each group's sheets were transcribed into a table of every figure, with its tolerance or fit and how sure the reading is (sure: legible, likely: legible with one reading taken over another, unsure: faint or partly hidden). Where a number mattered, the sheet itself was cropped and enlarged, and the readings were corrected there (below).

Readings corrected against the sheets

Checked on the sheets while building, where the transcription read a figure or a feature wrongly ( readings; the transcriptions are left as written):

The readings corrected
  • Five frame sizes drawn at their tolerances' tops, now at their middles (29 October 2026, the owner's choice, found by the recipes' check, PLAN-recipes.md): the barrel bridge's thickness 3.32 −0.04 (05 08 05-1) drawn 3.30; the fusee bush's flange Ø 13.2 −0.2 (05 08 01-2) Ø 13.1; the dust bush's body Ø 13.1 −0.2, collar Ø 15.1 −0.2 and neck Ø 9.7 −0.2 (05 08 01-3) Ø 13.0, 15.0 and 9.6. The model's convention draws a toleranced size at its middle, as it does the plates, the pillars and the fits; these five were drawn at their figures' tops. The collar at 15.1 was more than its Rundmessing 15 gives; at 15.0 it is the bar's own. With them: the dust bush's bottom keeps its figured 0.5 bearing ring inside the 0.3 × 45° chamfer (estimated), so the ring runs Ø 11.4-12.4; its collar's flat stays flush with the body (14.1, read 14.1 −0.2, at its middle 14.0 from the far side); the cork ring's bore stays the neck's + 0.01 (Ø 9.62). dims.js (WD.BB, FB, DB, CORK) holds each with its tolerance.
  • The up-and-down wheel's "35,3 −0,2" (05 02_11; 28 October 2026, the second drawing check's F3): its arrows lie on the outermost circle, which is the tip circle (its ratio to the rim's inside 1.206 against D/28.2's 1.217 and 35.3/28.2's 1.252; an overlay lays the model's tips on it), so 35,3 is the blank's diameter, as 05 02_7's "21,5 gedreht" and 05 02_9's "20,2 gedreht" run over their tables' D; the tips are the table's D 34,33, as built (a 35.3 tip would cut 0.45 into the pinion's root at 18.4).
  • The dial's seconds hole "17" (05 02_12; the same, F7): its arrows are drawn outside, pointing in to extension lines tangent to the hole (the small-hole convention, the hole drawn oversize at about 2.0), so the hole is Ø 1,7, as built round the collet's Ø 1.5; not 2.2 (Lange's 1453/A).
  • 05 02_1's framed 2,6 and 3,2, and its "2,8" (the same, F1, F5, 7-M5): the 2,6 is the dial's top face to the hour hand's top and the 3,2 the dial's top face to the minute hand's underside, at the cannon tube's square's shoulder (the transcription had them on the cannon's fit and the dial's underside); the "28°" by the fusee arbor is its Ø 2,8 in the plate. 05 02_06's "4,3 +0,1" runs to the pinion's underside, and 05 02_1's "0,6" is the change wheel's collar (F2, F4): the code had them right; the transcription is corrected.
  • The winding square "3,1 r6" (28 October 2026, the second drawing check's 5-M1): 05 06 04-1's figure after "3," is the hand's flagged 1 (the 1 of "+0,015" beside it is drawn alike), and +0.023/+0.015 is r6 for 3-6 mm; with 3.12 at the root the 1:100 over the square's 20.3 gives the sheet's own 2,92 at the point. Read "3,17 r6" until then (the transcription's), 0.05 too large. The dust plate's "3,1 □ H7, Kegel 1:100" then wedges 1.0 from the root, where 05 06_1 dimensions it (built 4.0 off, its hole straight 3.134 and loose, until then: 5-M2); the key's socket (05 01 02-3: 3.1 +0.05, drawn 3.15) takes the square anywhere along it.
  • The body's sixth "Grund" radius, 10,07 (28 October 2026, the second drawing check's 5-M13, closed): both issues of the body (05 06 04-2 and 02-1) read 10,07, the 7's stroke matching the column's other 7s; 05 06_20 reads 10,04, but it is a steel fusee's curve ("Schneckenkurve von Stahlschnecke"), not this part's sheet. Built 10.07; the 0.03 recorded.
  • The 1941 arbor's square end (28 October 2026, the second drawing check's 4-M5, kept). 0207's section ends the square 10 past the barrel bridge's outer face, rounded, with no point; the model's as first drawn runs its sides to y −35.4 and a point to −37.32, 1.65 further. Kept: 020704-1 (the arbor's own sheet) gives 7 + 22,2 + 15 = 44,2 overall with a turning centre on the square's end, and Wempe 3955's photograph (4_Wempe_3955_N.jpg) shows the point, 2.2 ±0.3 high, its sides ending 13.1 from the shoulder; 0207's ends are schematic (its plate end a ball where 020704-1 has a centre).
  • The chain's top hook's "30°" (28 October 2026, the second drawing check's 4-M20, kept with its reason). 05 07 04 draws the nose's inner edge about 50° to the chain's line (45° to its drawn throat wall, which leans 5°: the comparer's and the refuter's readings; 53-56° read again at 6×), and its "30°" arc is centred on the seat with one arm on the throat wall. The sheet's own figures leave no room for that edge: with the seat r 0,4 at 3,5 from the rivet (its figure, drawn at 3.0), the throat wall 1,8 in from the outer edge and the nose ending 2 from the rivet, 2.5 across, the only line from the nose's end tangent to the seat on the throat's side lies at 30.1° to the chain's line (at 50° the seat would have to stand 2.6 from the rivet, at 45° 2.76). So the figures, with their 30° read to the chain's line, are built; the drawing's steeper edge goes with its seat drawn at 3.0, before the bold "3,5" (likely a revised figure). An edge drawn at 50° would break the 3,5 or the 2.
  • The 1946 staff's rollers, and with them the escapement's heights as last revised (27 October 2026, from Unresolved, the owner's question on the banking screw). 05 04 02 (29.5.46) dimensions from the hub's flange top: the hub's neck to 4.1 +0.05, then a step to 5.6, then the lower arm. Measured on the sheet at 17.6 px/mm (its Ø 1.65 at the top, 29 px), the step is 28 px wide (Ø 1.6-1.65) and the arm under it 21 px (Ø 1.2); a Ø 2.14 would be 38 px. The step is therefore the "1,65 s6" seat, its leader drawn to it, and the "2,14 +0.01" is the hub's bore at its foot. The impulse roller (02 04 02: 1.6 thick, bored 1.627/1.65 on 1:70) sits on that seat from the hub's end, and the discharge roller under it on the Ø 1.2 r6. Four sources agree:
    • 05 03_3.2, the production staff of 13.3.65: its Ø 1.65 −0.02 seat 1.6 long, from 4.1 to 5.7.
    • The coloured section, which numbers its staff and hub 05 04 02-1 and -2: the impulse roller directly under the hub's end, about 4.2 under the flange top, the discharge roller under it, at 9.4 px/mm.
    • 05 04_1's "4,1 bis Unruhauflage".
    • Wempe No. 9166 of 1972 (Uhren-Hidding's archive, uhren-hidding.de/326-xxlarge/marinechronometer-chronometerwerke-wempe.jpg, a side view under the balance): the escape wheel's teeth right under the top plate, the detent along the plate, the block's upright under it with the slotted head at the stone (sure in layout); its balance rim close over the plate, about 0.3-0.5 by the rim's 3.8, as the model's 0.45 (likely). Wempe 9411 (Auktionshaus Stahl 113478) looks the same at low resolution. The model had read a collar Ø 2.14 from 4.1 to 5.6 with the impulse roller under it, which put the rollers 1.5 lower than every other source. To meet them it put the escape wheel 1.5 lower (its arbor's ends 0.49 and 0.06 inside the plates), read the block's side view in third angle (the upright flush with the plate, the detent's foot 3.2-5.2), left the banking screw a shank bearing on nothing, and listed the conflict as Unresolved. Now the rollers stand 0.32-3.52 under the plate and the escape wheel's teeth 0.4-1.8, its arbor's ends 1.98 and 1.55 in. The block is 05 04 01-4 read in first angle as the sheet reads, built as the escapement of 1943's, its banking screw whole and the pipe on its head. The detent's foot is at 1.3-3.2, its pipe 1.9-3.8, the lower endstone 1.5 down a window in its setting. The balance, its staff's other figures and every plan stay; makeEsc and the physics are planar, so the escapement's timing doesn't move with the heights (the bodies' inertias do, slightly: wempe_inertia.json). The owner chose not to keep the old reading as a version (27 October 2026).
  • The detent's blade flush toward its block (27 October 2026, the owner's choice "Adopt and refit"; .1436's left view and 10-2's "linke Seite": sure): the foot, spring, square and the blade's thicker part are centred 0.11 ((0,50 − 0,28)/2) off the blade's line toward the wheel, the blade, pipe and stone flush with their face toward the block (the blade centred until then). The block's offset 0.30 → 0.19 (ACR 7.49), so the stone lands 18.77 from the block's screw row (18.73), the detent line turns 0.15°, its flexure lies 0.11 off the stone's line, the gold spring's bending point 0.11 over. The discharge stone's reach (estimated, set so the stone is lifted 0.07 past the lock) takes the gold spring's tip's slide out along the blade as the detent turns about the offset flexure, DOFF times the turn (2.6 µm): RD 1.578 (1.5754 without it, which lifted the tip 12 µm less, let the stone fall back 0.6° sooner onto the tooth's tip with a weak drive, makeEsc's swing 78° at 90 %, and held the swing on the stone's blow's step). The detent weighed about the offset flexure: ID 8.23 (8.16), the 6MX's 8.01 (7.94). The swing 197.1° at 12 h (195.1°), 192.4-202.3° over the wind; HS −0.483 at it (−0.470). Two cross-checks widened, the owner's choice (The physics pass).

Bowditch's probable error of a fix (±2 miles) is taken as a circular normal whose median radius is 2 miles (σ 1.70 a side); Bowditch gives the figure, not its distribution.
  • The detent's knock margin: since 19 October 2026's physics pass, with the estimated 0.8 g preload, a 3 ms blow across the plate of 25.6 g lets a tooth go on the frame as drawn (22.6 g at 0.8 times, 28.7 g at 1.2 times; the knock's floor under 0.64 g, below the margin's 0.78 g, which the bench takes). Before it (18 October 2026), with the estimated 0.63 g preload, a 3 ms blow across the plate of 20.4 g lets a tooth go on the frame as drawn (20.0-20.1 g before the horn was traced) (tripping.js --model wempe, its least-knock search refined from six halvings to ten: the coarse one read 22 g). The check asks 20 g or more, so the margin is a hair at the estimate. The model keeps the estimate; the bench takes the knock's floor, 0.61 g, as a second least beside the margin's 0.51 (the user's choice), its window 0.61-1.55 g aimed near 0.84 g, where the 3 ms blow wants about 25 g (the line through the frame's runs carried on past 1.2 times: estimated).

  • The threads' form (26 October 2026): the sheets give each thread's size (M2.6, M2, M1.7, M1.4, M1.2), not its form or fit, and no photograph in the set shows a loose screw's thread. Every screw's shank is drawn as a right-hand ISO metric thread at its size's coarse pitch (ISO 261/262, DIN 13; M1.7 0.35, M2.6 0.45: KIT.isoP), ISO 68-1's basic profile (60°, the depth 0.541 p, flats p/8 and p/4), at 6g's maximum material (its major diameter less es = 15 + 11p µm: an allowance of 7.5 + 5.5p µm on the radius), run out to its root over the pitch before its 45° tip. A size the sources leave estimated keeps its estimate (the case's M3-M6, the 6MX's contact's). The tapped holes of the frame (the plates', bridges', cocks' and bushes' tables, the pillars' ends, the detent block's M1.7 and the wire spring's stud's hole 5) carry the inside thread at 6H's minimum (the basic profile), running out over a pitch to the drilled hole at each face, so screw and hole are the allowance apart radially all round; each screw is turned on its axis to lie on its hole's helix (KIT.matchThreads: 43 screws in all the versions). Other tapped holes (the movement ring's, the dial screws' in its flange, the fusee's, the balance's masses', the case's and the 6MX's contact's) stay plain bores at the thread's size and 0.02, the screws in them threaded. Standard practice, not read off a Wempe: sure of the sizes, estimated in form and fit.
